articleTitle: Design of LISP-Based Processors
Statistical Multiplexing Of Low-Speed Digitized Voice And Data Channels
abstract: Typical problems related to the integration of digitized voice and data traffic into general purpose networks are outlined. A particular solution is presented in the case of a transparent intelligent network (CODEX 6000 Series Intelligent Network Processors) where data traffic and low speed digitized voice (TSP 2400 bps VOCODER) are statistically multiplexed. Performances were analyzed using network supplied statistics as well as external measurements under variable conditions of data/voice mix, data traffic burstiness, number of hops and circuit character istics. Some typical applications are then described and their economics discussed.

articleTitle: Virtual Machine Technology: A Bridge From Large Mainframes To Networks Of Small Computers
abstract: The cost effectiveness of small computers (minis and micros) makes it desirable to use networks of such machines in a manner that provides the functionality available on large systems, but takes advantage of the potentially greater reliability of a distributed system. This paper explores how traditional virtual machine concepts can be extended to networks of cooperating virtual machines running on multiple processors. Some design approaches useful in building systems of cooperating virtual machines are then discussed.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Implementation Of A Linear Predictive Coder
abstract: This paper describes a linear predictive coder (LPQ and its microprocessor fabrication. The LPC has an audio bandwidth of 3200 Hz, uses the autocorrelation formulation of LPC to determine the short term spectrum, and an Average Magni- tude Difference Function (AMDF) to extract pitch. A two multiplier/stage lattice filter at the receiver recreates the speech. The 2400 b/s full duplex LPC is implemented in the firmware of a horizontally coded microprocessor having a 48-bit instruction word and 16-bit data word. The processor architecture uses a 4-bit TTL ALU slice and a hardwared 16 x 16 bit parallel multiplier to rapidly process the data with relatively slow multiplication circuitry. With the chosen architecture, the LPC requires only 60 percent of the proces sor's capacity, while the processor itself has fewer than 150 integrated components. The low cost of the voice digitizer has resulted in commercial sales in a market that appears to be growing.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of System Features for the MC60000
abstract: The MC613000 combines state-of-the-art technology, advanced circuit design techniques, and computer science to achieve an architecturally advanced 16-bit microprocessor. The processor is implemented by a microprogrammed control of an execution unit. The processor incorporates advanced system features, including multi-level vectored interrupts, privilege states. illegal instruction policing, and bus cycle abort. This paper discusses the implementation of the system features and the influence of the implementation method on the processor design.

articleTitle: On-line Fault Detection And Correction In Microprocessor Systems
abstract: In most on-line diagnostic schemes whenever a fault is detected in a system, a rather involved system recovery routine is initiated irrespective of whether the fault is caused by a failure inside a chip, or by a failure outside a chip, say, on the bond connecting a pin to the chip. Failures of the latter type cause errors only when some information is being transferred from one chip to another chip. In this paper, 'two new techniques to system recovery are described for the case when an error is on any such data transfer path. These schemes are implementable locally, and the system is ensured to recover from any single stuck-at fault, single AND-bridge fault, or single OR-bridge fault in a single retry. The system- recovery from faults internal to chips can be per- formed using sophisticated routines. Thus, two- level approach to on-line system diagnosis seems to be more efficient.

articleTitle: A Microprocessor-based Module To Provide Security In Electronic Funds Transfer Systems
GUMBI - A Graphic User Microprogrammable Bit-slice Interpreter
abstract: A microprograrmned bit-slice graphic interpreter, designed to be the front end for a frame store display system, is described. High-speed operation, in conjunction with user programmability, yields a powerful, general purpose tool suitable for a wide range of graphic/picture processing applications.

articleTitle: Cryptographic Pin Processing In EFT Systems
abstract: A described method of protecting Personal Identification Numbers (PINS) assumes the Point of Sale (POS) terminal is online to a host operating system and that both terminal and host have a cryptographic capability based upon the DES al- gorithm and support a cryptographic key management scheme.1 Subscription by the host and terminal to a communications protocol which can support end-to-end encryption, 2 provides additional security. In this environment a table of user PINS, indexed by user name, is maintained at the host. By permitting customer PIN verification at either the terminal or the host when a transaction is initiated, an exhaustive attack against the PIN becomes as difficult as one against a DES key.

articleTitle: TheLSI-11/23 Control Store Microarchitecture
abstract: The LSI-11/23, an LSI version of Digital Equipment's PDP-11/34, is the first microcomputer with the performance and features of a midrange minicomputer. Three forty-pin packages containing five NMOS LSI chips form the basis for a complete CPU on an 5" x 8" board with extensive memory management features and both single and double precision floating point instructions (see Figure 1) . This paper describes one of the features, the control store and control sequencer*, that enabled the LSI-11/23 to obtain two and a half times the performance of the LSI/11, while maintaining a flexible microarchitecture for instruction set extensions.

articleTitle: Microprocessors And Data Encryption
abstract: The use of microprocessors for implementing some of the new public cryptographic algorithms is examined. Time and space requirements for the various encryption programs are studied and applications where microprocessor based encryption would be able to meet throughput requirements are identified. It is concluded that with currently available microprocessors, micro-based encryption is useful for offline encryption/decryption, electronic mail systems, and most terminal applications.

articleTitle: Data management for microcomputers
A Direct Execution Processor
On-Line Image Enhancement In The Time Domain With A Microprocessor
abstract: It might seem that image enhancement by histogram transformation of video pictures in real-time would be a very demanding task requiring a high performance computer. However, by setting up the two speed critical, but computationally simple, tasks of histogram gathering and image transformation as semi-independent subsystems con- trolled by a microprocessor, while leaving the computationally intensive task of determining the transformation to the microprocessor, it becomes possible to perform video enhancement dynamically by simple, inexpensive means. Histogram gathering and image transformation go on continually. During the vertical blank of every field, the con- tents of histogram memory are accumulated in main memory and zeroed to avoid premature saturation. After accumulating histogram data for one or more fields, a new transformation function is computed during the next frame, and loaded into the image transformation RAM during the vertical blank pre- ceding the following frame, when the new function becomes effective. The algorithm used for this computation is described, and is applicable to both histogram equalization and histogram hyperbolization. The system was built and tested, demonstrating considerable improvement in visual clarity. Particularly impressive results were obtained when a rectangular window was applied to areas of interest showing poor contrast. The enhancement obtained is illustrated by comparing input and output video pictures.

articleTitle: Japanese Word Processor JW-10
Answer Search Interface (ASI)
abstract: The functions of a microprocessor are incorporated as one partner in an air traffic control dialog for ground control by the ASI and its peripherals. Of the input speech signals less than 30% are filtered and extracted as "Key Features of Content (KFC) by comparison with hardwired KFCs- After their actualization they are used to trigger signals for prepared discrete answers in the Answer Search Logic. This is substantialized by a hardwired sequential network in analogy to natural language content.

articleTitle: Interprocessor Communication In Multiprocessor Simulation Systems
Microcontroller For Exhaust-Stack Environmental Measurements/sup */
Floating Point Standardization
Communications In A Hierarchical Multicomputer
abstract: This paper describes the design of the hardware and the basic functions of the operating system for a tree organized multicomputer now being constructed in the Computer Science deptartment at Stony Brook. The processors have separate local memories and are interconnected by communication links specialized for the transfers of short control type messages and large blocks of data. Also discussed is the influence of previous simulation studies and the operating system considerations on the design of the hardware and interprocessor communication protocols.

articleTitle: A microprocessor-based design of the data base computer
abstract: Initial investigation found that the original Data Base Computer approach to be most appealing in light of Sperry Univac's need to support existing customers' data bases and applications while at the same time offering them cost/performance improvement and additional capabilities. A revised architecture was designed that offered the benefits sought at a price and level of complexity that is extremely attractive. Improvements to the design to aid in recovery operations and the performance modeling should be complete by the time this paper is published. The result should be a special purpose computer design that could significantly improve the users ability to mange the ever growing body of data characteristic of our modern technological society.

articleTitle: A Microcomputer-based Speech Recognition System
Microprocessors In Aerospace Applications
abstract: The age of microprocessors is upon the aerospace industry. Giant strides have been taken by the semiconductor industry in the development of microprocessors in recent days, and in so doing, they have provided us with both a challenge and an opportunity to pursue an almost unlimited number of potential applications. As one looks through the areas of business of today's aerospace company, the products almost look like a catalog of micro- processor applications, and indeed, they are. Guidance and control, missile guidance, inertial navigation, avionic systems, torpedo systems, flight controls, engine controls, sonar systems and digital test systems are certainly prime candidate areas for the application of micro- processors. This paper essentially surveys a limited number of state-of-the-art microprocessor applications within such an aerospace company, specifically, within The Bendix Corporation. Throughout this discussion, it is essential for our perspective to recall, however, that we have only just uncovered the tip of the iceberg. Remember, microprocessors have only recently been introduced into the aerospace industries' end products.

articleTitle: Design Of A Fault-Tolerant Microprocessor
abstract: Following an overview of the general practice in the reliable design of digital systems and the discussion of those design considerations for selfchecking and fault tolerant machines, the Self- Checking Microprocessor proposed by Maki (3) is brought to the readers' attention. Then the posibility of using this self-checking design in a hybrid-redundant microprocessor system is explored. In this paper, the self-checking processor and the main memory unit are triplicated for the purposeof error detection and momentary fault masking. Reconfiguration, allowing stand by units to replace failed unit, is possible due to the intelligence of the individual processors. Similarly the memory modules can be switched ON/OFF line by an additional self-checking processor incorporated into the design assuming the task of the majority voter of this TMR system.

articleTitle: Microprocessor Implementations Of Discrete Fourier Transform Machines
abstract: When computing the Fourier Transform with a microprocessor, the speed and complexity of the algorithm which is used become especially important. The most frequently used algorithm has been the Fast Fourier Transform. More recently developed algorithms require fewer multiplications and about the same number of additions as the FFT. A comparison of these algor ithms is made and some possible structures of machines are suggested. A description of a machine built to use one of the new algorithms is given and the problems which were encountered are discussed.

articleTitle: A Multiple Microprocessor-Based Nuclear Reactor Power Monitor
Chinese Character Input/Output And Transmission In Japanese Personal Computing
A Microprocessor-Based Multi-loop Network System
abstract: A microprocessor-based multi-loop network system (MLNET) has been developed. MLNET has been designed to be a flexible and reliable low cost local network suitable for small systems. MLNET consists of many nodes and a number of communication loops, whose control is distributed all over the nodes to increase its reliability. This paper describes MLNET, emphasizing on details of its network topology, intra-loop transmission and inter-loop communication schemes, and its hardware and software.

articleTitle: Scientific calculating peripheral
abstract: A scientific calculating peripheral for small intelligent data acquisition and instrumentation systems and for distributed-task processing systems is established with a number-oriented microprocessor controlled by a single component universal peripheral interface microcontroller. A MOS/LSI number-oriented microprocessor provides the scientific calculating capability with Reverse Polish Notation data format. Master processor task definition storage, input data sequencing, computation processing, result reporting, and interface protocol is managed by a single component universal peripheral interface microcontroller.

articleTitle: Spacelab Payloads Standard Multi-processor Computer System
Static Assignment Of Processes To Microcomputers In A Dedicated Application
abstract: The static assignment of predefined processes to a set of similar microcomputers for use in a process control application is considered. The goal is to minimize the number of computers required. A general solution is presented which involves solving a sequence of packing problems. A faster, suboptimal technique is also presented together with suggestions for its application.

articleTitle: A Non-Least-Squares Criterion For Speech Coding
CHAMIL A Case Study in Microprogramming Language Design
Microprocessor System Testing And Diagnostics
A Single-chip 4-BIT Microcomputer: MN1500 Series
abstract: In recent years single-chip microcomputers have been increasingly applied to consumer product controllers and various machine controllers. In this paper, a high performance single-chip 4-bit microcomputer is described which mainly processes 4-bit data and has some instructions processing 8-bit data.

articleTitle: Microprocessors Applied To Minicomputers
abstract: A one card bit slice microprocessor based CPU emulation of an existing family of high speed, general purpose, aerospace processors is presented. This high performance bit slice microprocessor based machine provides the high speed computational capability necessary to satisfy a broad spectrum of real time system applications. Specific existing applications for this machine include use as the guidance and control computer for an advanced missile system, as the processing element in a fault tolerant network and as an embedded processor. The objectives of this emulation is to improve overall performance characteristics while maintaining software compatibility with the emulated family of processors. In addition, the resulting bit slice microprocessor should be upwards software compatible with its predecessors (having a powerful expanded instruction set with improved performance). The design objectives were aimed at a real time high performance processor architecture. Hardware which implements this emulation has been built and tested, verifying the desired improvements. The resulting machine is completely software compatible with its predecessors, and also contains a powerful expanded instruction set. As an example of the performance improvement achieved, the interregister add execution time is less than 250 nanoseconds, as compared with one microsecond for the predecessor machines. An overall improvement in throughput greater than three-to- one has been demonstrated for this processor (specifically, the throughput exceeds 1 MIPS*) without considering the additional efficiency obtainable through the use of the expanded instruction set. Additional design goals and improvements which have been obtained include: (a) half the weight, size and power dissipation, (b) reduced cost, (c) increased

articleTitle: A Control Architecture For Distributed Processing Systems
Communications Processor Architecture: A Microprocessor Design
abstract: The Communications Processor Architecture is implemented In tbe Sperry Univac r DCP/40 /spl sub (1), and is targeted towards high performance secure operation and network functionality. The architecture supports the utilization of large scale integration, microprocessors and microprogramming in every module. In addition to providing functionality and performance in the communications environment, the DCP/40 provides excellent general purpose processing capability. increased performance is achieved through advanced components and functional distribution of tasks among the various processing elements. Security and integrity is attained through address and queue access protection. As a unique feature of the architecture, all I/0 is treated in common whether it drives peripheral devices or communications lines. This technique simplifies software as well as hardware design.

articleTitle: A Loosely Coupled Microprocessor Network For Underground Coal Mines
Current And Future Developments In Flexible Disk Technology
An Architecture For A Unified System Of Coordinated Microcomputers
abstract: This paper discusses the architecture of the Microprogrammable Controller (MPC), a unified system of 50 coordinated intel 808OA-based microcomputers using a bus for communications. The MPC implements a solution for the problem of coordinating a large array of microcomputers oper -ating in an asynchronous, parallel manner. The MPC architecture provides high performance and fault tolerance. The raw port-to-port transfer rate is 250K bits per second with response time being insensitive to the load on the system. Partial configurations within the MPC are tolerated, and errors in one portion of the system are localized, causing no long term degradation in system performance. The MPC is currently in use as a console controller and communications front end for a system consisting of two large mainframes and 48 consoles. The MPC hardware consists of interface processors, called ports, connected to a demand driven multiple access (DDMA) bus. The DDMA bus is a six-foot long, 16-bit parallel bus with a one microsecond cycle. The bus grants access to the ports on a cycle-by-cycle, rotating priority basis. There are four port types: two types of console ports, serial communications interface ports, and management and coordination ports. Each port contains its own local memory and I/O interface with no global memory attached to the bus. The MPC software consists of multiple, functionally-oriented subsystems. The interport communications (IPC) and system management and coordination (SMC) subsystems will be discussed in some detail. The IPC software provides the basic operating system for the other subsystems of the MPG. IPC is a totally distributed subsystem which enforces a uniform flexible protocol for all port to-port communications within the MPC. SMC is primarily responsible for coordination with the mainframes and provides support for the setup and breakdown of console sessions. This architecture presents a viable solution for a long range of problems involving multipro processing and multiprocessor systems.

articleTitle: LSI Bubble Memory Controller
A Microprocessor Based Simultaneous Voice And Data Network Processor
abstract: Microprocessors are utilized throughout a distributed processing system to implement a mixed digital voice and data network. A multi- processor architecture and multi- tasking operating system enforce modularity in both the hardware and software. An integrated voice and data service combines all point- to-point communications needs, pro- viding optimal use of expensive leased lines. This control structure gives the user many network features including automatic channel contention, remote network reconfiguration on operator command or automatically by time of day, graphics display of current network status, and statistical multiplexing of voice, data, and control to further reduce bandwidth requirements.

articleTitle: A High Density Bubble Memory System
MAC-4: A Single-Chip Microcomputer
Time-sharing And Interuser Communications For The Personal Computer Market
Utilization of Rams With a Defective Row or Column In Micros and Minis
Distributed Telephone Switching System
Design Principles of Structure-Independent Operating Systems for Multi-Microprocessor Systems
Programming for the LK3000 and Cartridges
Microprocessors: Their Management And Use In Low Cost Applications
The Micro Computer Controlled UV Ozone Calibrator
HP300 Architecture
abstract: The HP300 is a low cost computer system whose CPU is a stack processor with separate non-modifiable segmented code spaces plus additional virtual memory segmented data spaces. The stack is used for program control, paramenter passing, local storage and expression evaluation. The data segments provide space for global data and additional array space. Capabilities provided by this structure include relocatability, reentrancy, recursion, code sharing, program protection, convenient dynamic storage allocation, and a logical virtual memory structure for code and data that provides a large machine address space. The CPU is a microprogram controlled processor utilizing three costom-designed large-scale integrated (LSI) circuits, 6K 32-bit words of read-only memory control store and some periphera logic to communicate through the intermodule bus to memory and I/0. The LSI circuits are made with HP's complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor/ silicon-on sapphire (CMOS/SOS) process. The CPU architecture and hardware design are described in this paper.

articleTitle: Computer-Assisted Translation Mainframe To Microprocessor
Real-time Vocoder Hardware: Past, Present And Future
abstract: The design of hardware which implements real-time analysis/synthesis telephony (commonly referred to as VOCODER's) has been heavily influenced by the prevailing limits of electronic technology. The current explosion of capability made possible by LST techniques is once again changing the way the game is played. This paper traces this evolutionary process through the current state of the art -- the bipolar "bit-slice" microcomputer approach -- and suggest some ways in which future signal-processing systems may be implemented.

articleTitle: Development Of A "Higher-Level" Microprogramming Language Using A Compiler-Compiler
abstract: A non-traditional microprogramming language and its development using a compiler-compiler are described. An idea of the synergism that can develop between more user-oriented microprogramming tools, well-organized hard- ware architecture, and compiler-compiler syntax structure is presented. Considering the characteristics of the resulting product, the effort involved in this implementation methodology seems to have been well-spent.

articleTitle: Structured Control At Machine Instruction Level
Color Graphic Design System for IC Mask
abstract: A Color Graphic Design System for IC mask pattern (called CGDS) is described. The main CGOS aims are as follow. Short response time Improvement in operation capability In order to realize these two aims, CGDS is made up of some attractive special 1/0 devices, such as an interactive color graphic terminal, an automatic drawing recognition system, a large size electrostatic plotter and a color film recorder. The interactive color graphic terminal has raster scan color displays, very large image memory and many graphic hardware units. So, in this terminal, very quick response is realized with each layer IC mask displaying in different colors. Using this terminal, man-machine interactive operation in IC mask design would be very easy and designer's operation errors would be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Bootstrapping Implementation Of Compilers For A Microcomputer
Pascal Microengine
A/D LSI Controller Peripheral Chip
A Component For Multimicrocomputer Structures : A Programmable Arbiter
abstract: Low cost microprocessors promote the design of structures in which tasks are decentralized on several processors. in such structures, shared resources (memories, arithmetical modules...) are accessed by means of bus controllers. This paper describes a centralized bus controller (also called Arbiter module) which is programmable and considered as a component of a microprocessor family it allows a large number of allocation algorithms.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based Transition Machines
Communications Protocol for a Building Automation System
abstract: With the advent of microprocessors, it has become economical to distribute some of the building automation system (BAS) functions, once reserved for centralized minicomputers. With this comes a need for an efficient and economical communications protocol. Of chief concern in a BAS system are system response times and information throughput. Standard protocols (e.g. SDLC, HDLC, ADCCP, X.25, CAMAC) are general purpose protocols with high overheads. The high overheads associated with these protocols makes their use inefficient in a BAS. This paper describes the design considerations and tradeoffs in the design of JCI's proprietary BAS protocol. This protocol is a byte oriented, variable length polling protocol intended for use in several levels of distributed BAS networks.

articleTitle: Security Design Issues For Microprocessor-Based Systems
abstract: This paper examines some representative applications for using microprocessor technology with the intent of identifying potential multilevel security requirements and design approaches for satisfying these requirements with micropro- cessor-based systems. The discussion focuses on design issues that are unique to the development of secure microprocessor-based systems and related difficulties in transferring designs for secure mini- and maxi-based systems to microprocessors.

articleTitle: Impact Of Winchester Technology On Small Systems
abstract: Winchester technology has emerged as the leader for meeting the fixed media magnetic disk storage requirements of large systems. However, its success in the small systems arena has been minimal to date. This is mainly due to the availability of cost-effective storage devices implemented with removable media disk drives, based on IBM 5440 cartridge and CDC Storage Module technologies. In this paper, the storage requirements of small systems are characterized and related to the attributes of existing and future disk storage technologies. Systems level analysis is given to avoid "apples and oranges" type comparisons. Accordingly, for applications requiring back up of stored information for safety or archival purposes, the impact of the back-up device is included in any comparison such as cost, reliability and maintainability.

articleTitle: The S100 Bus: Where do we go from here?
abstract: The general system characteristics of the IEEE S100 bus specification are discussed, particularly in relation to S100 bus suitability in a closely coupled multiprocessor system. System throughput is modelled and a number of alternate architectures for multiprocessing are discussed in relation to trends in semiconductor and software technology.

articleTitle: Small Disk = Large Capacity
abstract: The 5-1/4" floppy disk drive was introduced in 1976 as a low cost alternative to the 8" IBM standard flexible disk drive. Originally aimed at the blossoming small business and personal computer industry, these small, low-cost drives offered a maximum unformatted data capacity of only 110 kbytes. Although the 5-1/4" floppy is now 2 years old, most drives being shipped by the handfull of 5-1/4" floppy manufacturers is still capable of only 110 kbytes of storage. Because of the popularity of the 5-1/4" floppy and increased demand for storage by the suppliers of microcomputer systems, most of these manufacturers are now trying to increase the capacity of their drives by in creasing bit density (using MFM or M2FM recording techniques) and/or using double sided heads. One manufacturer, however, Micropolis Corporation, Canoga Park, California, has been offering a drive since the spring of 1977 which provide 4.4 times the normal density on a single side of a standard 5-1/4" diskette. First available only in disk memory subsystems, Micropolis' 480 kbyte unformatted capacity drive is now supplied, on an OEM basis, to many microcomputer system manufacturers. Originally viewed as a novelty, the drive is now widely accepted as a highly reliable alternative to other low capacity 5-1/4" drives. Micropolis expects to ship nearly 20,000 drives over the next year. The double-sided Micropolis drive now being supplied in evaluation quantities is capable of I megabyte of storage per drive! How has Micropolis been able to offer so much more capacity? The drive mechanism incorporated two technologies already well-proven in the peripheral industry yet not then introduced to 5-1/4" floppy design: Increased Bit Density ------ MFM Data Recording Increased Track Density ---- 100 Tracks per inch (77 tracks total) MFM (Modified Frequency Modulation) increases the nominal capacity of 110 kbytes to 220 kbytes. The increase from 35 tracks to 77 tracks yields 77/35 X 220 = 480 kbytes.

articleTitle: Voice Remote Controlled Tv Set
A CAM-Augmented Mico-Based Relational Data Base
abstract: This paper proposes a CAM-augmented micro-computer as a relational "data base machine". Relational algebra primitives are defined and their implementation on a CAM is discussed. It is demonstrated that set and and relational operations may be performed in linear time.

articleTitle: Micro-Seed And Its Application
abstract: Micro-SEED is the first complete database management system for microcomputers. This paper reviews the development of Micro-SEED and then describes two applications that have been developed to use Micro-SEED: general ledger and bill-of-material processors. A final section evaluates the performance of Micro-SEED in terms of the transaction rate of general ledger applications that can be supported and calculates the cost per transaction.

articleTitle: INTEL/sup R/ 8090 I/0 Processor Enhances Microcomputer System Performance
abstract: I/0 subsystems play a key role in affecting the performance of computer systems. Intelligent I/0 subsystems have been effectively used by main- frame and minicomputer manufacturers in improving overall system performance. The Intel 8089 I/0 processor enhances the performance of microcomputer systems such as the 8086 and 8088 by supporting intelligent I/0 subsystems that significantly increase system throughput. The paper discusses system architectures employing the I/0 processor, the CPU-IOP communication scheme and the internal processor architecture.

articleTitle: A Bipolar Microprocessor Based Bubble Memory Controller
A Microcomputer Based Educational System With Dual Display
CPX - An Experimental Virtual Machine Monitor
Design of the Lexicon LK-3000 Language Computer
Standardization and Control of Microcomputer Systems Development in a Large Corporation
abstract: (Please refer to Section I - "Purpose and Outline"). 1. Purpose and Outline - Much has been written recently about the "maturing" of desk-top microcomputer system, as the user community migrates from the electronics hobbyist to the small businessman. At the same time, however, an equally significant, but less visible movement is occurring in industry, where many corporations are daily discovering new, cost effective applications for general-purpose microcomputer systems. Because these new computers are so inexpensive, a very real danger exists of uncontrolled proliferation in the corporate environment. Uncontrolled proliferation, in turn, leads directly to inefficient usage, duplication of effort and excessive costs. This paper relates the current attempt of one large corporation, The Boeing Company, to anticipate these problems and to put a solution in place BEFORE the situation becomes uncontrollable. The paper begins with background material on the MINIcomputer proliferation problem that preceded the microcomputer situation. Lessons learned from a study of the minicomputer problem led to the creation of a Microcomputer Evaluation Project. The management philosophy behind Boeing's effort to control microcomputer proliferation is discussed next, followed by a section devoted to the technological foundation of the entire control effort - the concept of "portable code." Next, the organizational structure of the Evaluation Project is presented, along with an overview of the individual tasks currently in progress. The paper concludes with a summary of comments regarding the control effort from the Boeing user community, followed by a "challenge" to other industrial users who may want to initiate a similar program.

articleTitle: The Craig Handheld Translate, And Personal Computer
A Cooperative Highly-available Multi-processor Architecture CHAMP
abstract: This paper describes a research effort to design and construct a computer hardware architecture capable of expanding to accommodate additional processing needs and sustaining massive hardware failures while still retaining a useable processing ability. The SRI proprietary architecture described here has been developed to use a large number of processors in an arbitrarily connected lattice. This architecture is called CHAMP for Cooperative Highly Available Multi-Processor. The reasoning behind, and the justification for, such a design is explored. CHAMP will to be programmed using a design methodology based on the M-module (model-driven module), which is an autonomous pro- reduction of components and pin count gram module containing a model, a set of values, and a set of procedures. The use of this methodology is explored along with its application to fault tolerance. Basic fault tolerance algorithms are described in relation to the CHAMP architecture. Hardware has been designed and constructed for an initial test of the concepts.

articleTitle: Software Development for Task-Oriented Multiprocessor Architectures
abstract: The recent advances in the integrated circuits technology have boosted the interest in task-oriented computer architechtures. The abailability of suitable microprocessors makes it affordable to combine many of them into powerful multiprocessor configurations. The high cost effectiveness of this kind of hardware, however is contradicted by disproportionale costs for the development of software. In this paper, the problems of software development are investigated for the context of small, low cost multiprocessor projects. The construction of a software support system, that is tailored to the particular architecture, is described. The development of a multiprocessor system for speech recognition (the Harpy Machine) is used as an example for demonstrating how such a software support system can be based on a general purpose time sharing system (UNIX) and its facilities.

articleTitle: Partitioning For Virtual Machine Efficiency
abstract: The virtual machine concept, enabling individual users to concurrently access a computer's resources, has long been accepted for business applications and utilized by software implementors. Current implementations of the virtual machine concept have been achieved almost exclusively through the use of software (e.g., virtual machine monitors) Use of the concept for high performance, application processes has been constrained by the overhead resulting from the software monitor. This includes time required for application process dispatch and communication between the associated virtual machines whenever cooperation is required to meet a system objective.

articleTitle: A Parallel Array Of Microprocessors - An Alternative Solution To Diffusion Problems
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of using a parallel, special-purpose-processor to solve diffusion problems. The system considered in an N- Dimensional Array of Microprocessors each of which provides an explicit solution of the diffusion equation at its own location. A master-slave architecture is used in which it has been demonstrated that private memory assignment offers a considerable advantage over a common memory array in terms of complexity and the tradeoff between interprocessor interference and memory reduction. For economic reasons all communication in the prototype is by means of serial links. The master-slave communication protocol is very specific with the joint aims of compactness and flexibility demonstrably achieved.

articleTitle: A Legal Roadmap For Personal Computing Software

This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.
